items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: you made the point that with Goldkette and with Liz Galleat and Lynn Whiteman, you were an arranger

ctx.x: Well, we were talking about your career, and you made the point that with Goldkette and with Liz Galleat and Lynn Whiteman, you were an arranger, and later at a certain point you were an orchestrator, not an arranger. Would you elaborate on that a little bit?

Yes. During the '20s I was -- I was an arranger to set up something, maybe some sort of a style, to contribute any way I could. They were willing to accept that, and I did my work as I thought best. In other words, they gave me a tune to arrange. When the business -- when it came to 19 -- in the 1930s, middle 1930s anyway -- I was told what to do.
